correctness.rationale: Independent odd/even coupon streams identify the exact event T_b >= T_a. Multiplying the coupon-completion mass by the other stream survival function yields an absolutely convergent geometric series and a finite rational inclusion-exclusion identity. The equal-part formula follows from exchangeability, with a strict l2-convolution bound and a Fourier-dominated Gumbel limit proving the precise 1/(8m) correction. Independent Gumbel limits yield the logistic crossover on the m/log(m) scale. The two-vertex part has a binomial-coefficient PGF evaluation. The standalone exact rational checker passed 190 assertions, comparing all 64 small part-size pairs against an independent Markov recursion; the infinity claims have independent analytic arguments.

originality.rationale: The finding is the combined, all-parameter simple-random-walk endpoint distribution on complete bipartite graphs with a sharp near-balanced logistic size window and balanced finite correction. The 1993/2022 uniform-endpoint classification does not calculate this law; the Myers-Wilf (2003) exact simultaneous coupon-completion probability supplies the equal-part tie input and is explicitly credited as prior. Classical coupon-collector Gumbel convergence supplies a limiting ingredient, but no inspected source states the graph-specific finite profile and size-imbalance classification together. Explicit implicit-coverage and unavailable-1993-text risks remain.
residual_risks: Full text of Lovasz-Winkler (1993) could not be inspected.
Other earlier coupon-collision asymptotics may contain the balanced 1/(4m) constant or an equivalent endpoint implication.
The logistic result uses a standard two-Gumbel difference, and its historical priority could have been established in a general race framework without using complete-bipartite terminology.
Independent expert validation has not been performed.

value.rationale: A complete finite rational probability formula for a graph-wide first-discovery endpoint event, a nondegenerate critical imbalance window of width m/log(m) with a logistic limit, and a sharp balanced finite-size correction supply structurally interpretable information beyond general endpoint-uniformity classification. The K_(2,b) central-binomial case resolves the thin-part extreme. The distinction between side totals and individual endpoints is important for cover-tour hitting location, and both scales are natural rather than arbitrary numerical slices.
